#17660. Volkwagen’s ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Sends 362 All-Electric Horsepower to the Front Wheels

Volkwagen’s ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept Sends 362 All-Electric Horsepower to the Front Wheels

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (384 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part.
  • Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch.
  • Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen’s EV push in America has skewed practical, for the most part. The ID.4 was a generic crossover, so close to an electric take on the Tiguan that VW is actually rebranding it as the ID. Tiguan. And the ID. Buzz, whimsical styling aside, is an electric van—a very expensive electric van. But VW has not abandoned its small, fun hatchback roots in Europe, and the German brand is continuing the celebration of the 50th anniversary of its GTI sub-brand with an EV: the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, which it will debut at the Essen Motorshow later this month.

The ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is an all-electric, track-ready, front-wheel drive hot hatch. VW shoehorned an electric drive system intended for larger RWD vehicles into the sub-compact ID. Polo GTI; that gives the concept outputs of 362 horsepower (up to 389 hp in short bursts) and 406 pound-feet of torque, a massive increase from the 223 hp and 214 lb-ft in the standard model.

In a recent development, the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept can hit a top speed of 149 mph, and it can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 4.7 seconds—quicker than a Golf GTI but not quite as quick as a gas-powered Golf R—with the launch control engaged.

This VW’s body is heavily modified from the standard model, as well. It features a two-door layout instead of four, flared fenders, and an enormous front splitter, diffuser, and rear wing. VW also stripped out the interior for track work by deleting the rear seat and cargo area. The two front seats are Recaro racing bucket seats with five-point harnesses, and the interior also has an integrated Tornado Red roll bar.

In a recent development, sadly, this is just a concept for now. Volkswagen has not committed to building an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and even if the brand did, it would be unlikely to be offered in the American market. VW did reveal a very cool ID. GTI concept back in 2023, which it has claimed will be more fun than the combustion-powered GTIs. And Volkswagen, pointedly, has not ruled out bringing that car to America—though getting the pricing and timing right in the U.S., with an unstable tariff situation and variable EV incentive climate, may prove tricky.

#17659. Early Americans spent over 10 hours making a single pumpkin pie

Early Americans spent over 10 hours making a single pumpkin pie

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table.
  • It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert.
  • For generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s the late 1700s, and a pumpkin sits on a colonial kitchen table. The flesh has been cooked until soft. But the hard part is still ahead. To turn the pumpkin into pie, the cook must mash it, scrape it, and force it through a sieve, separating smooth pulp from stubborn strings and fibers. There is no can of pumpkin puree. No food processor. Just the pumpkin, rudimentary kitchen tools, and a lot of elbow grease. The work could take hours, all for an eight-person dessert. An 1876 Fresh England cookbook, for example, instructed cooks to simmer pumpkin for six to eight hours, stirring frequently, before rubbing it through a colander.

It seems like an absurd amount of work for dessert. Pumpkin flesh doesn’t naturally break down into a silky puree. Cooking softens its tissues, but turning the squash into smooth filling requires additional mechanical work.

For generations, cooks solved the problem with heat and muscle. Eventually, factories took over the work of cooking and processing pumpkins into puree. But the solution didn’t stop there. Growers also turned to pumpkin varieties with naturally smoother, less fibrous flesh, making the job easier before the squash even reached the factory.

According to recent reports, pumpkin was an key food in North America long before Thanksgiving became a national holiday. Indigenous peoples cultivated and prepared the squash in many forms, and European colonists adopted pumpkins as a plentiful crop. Colonists adapted their own pie-making traditions to the abundant squash, incorporating pumpkin into sweet and savory pies. By the 17th century, recipes for pumpkin-filled pies were appearing in English cookbooks.

In 1796, the first known American cookbook, Amelia Simmons’s American Cookery, included a recipe for “Pompkin Pudding” made with cooked pumpkin, milk, eggs, and spices. Before the pumpkin could be combined with the other ingredients, the recipe called for it to be strained, separating fine pulp from tougher material.

Thanksgiving didn’t take shape as a national tradition until the mid-19th century. Pumpkins were harvested in the fall and could be stored through the colder months, making them a natural ingredient for a holiday associated with the autumn harvest.

Recent findings suggest that the story of the Pilgrims sitting down with Native Americans for the first Thanksgiving has some truth to it, too. In 1621, English colonists and members of the Wampanoag people did gather for a three-day harvest celebration. But the friendly, feel-good version passed down in schoolbooks leaves out a much more complicated history of colonialism and conflict.

It wasn’t until over two centuries later that Sarah Josepha Hale, a prominent magazine editor, campaigned for decades for a national holiday, and, in 1863, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed a national “day of Thanksgiving.” She believed a shared day of gratitude, centered on family and community, could help unite a country increasingly divided by political conflict.

Sources indicate that hale also helped popularize the foods associated with the holiday, promoting a traditional New England Thanksgiving menu through her magazine. Pumpkin pie was already a regional favorite, but as Thanksgiving spread nationally after the Civil War, the dessert became part of the broader American tradition.

Pumpkin pie became increasingly associated with the holiday meal during this era, drawing on its roots in Newly introduced England’s seasonal cooking traditions. Preparing it remained labor-intensive, and results varied.

Industrial food processing offered a solution to the labor-intensive process of making pumpkin pie. Factories could cook and mechanically break down pumpkin in large quantities, producing puree without requiring every household to repeat the tedious process. Canning transformed pumpkin from a seasonal ingredient demanding considerable preparation into a convenient product that could be stored and used when needed.

John Coupland, Ph.D., professor of food science at Penn State, describes the work involved in preparing pumpkin by hand as “astonishing.” Industrial processing made pie filling far more convenient, eliminating the need to cook, mash, and strain a pumpkin from scratch.

It also gave bakers a reliable starting point, helping make pumpkin pie more consistent and cementing its place at the Thanksgiving table.

Industry observers note that making pumpkin puree is more complicated than simply cooking the flesh until soft. Pumpkin cells are surrounded by walls containing materials such as cellulose, hemicellulose, and pectin. Cooking softens the tissue, while mechanical processing breaks it into smaller particles. Together, these processes help determine the puree’s texture and moisture.

In a recent development, the goal is a smooth puree that is neither watery nor full of tough fibers. The pumpkin variety matters, as do the heating conditions and mechanical methods used to break down its flesh.

Modern food processing allows manufacturers to control these variables on a large scale, producing batches with similar textures and moisture levels. That predictability is especially valuable in pumpkin pie, where the filling’s consistency helps determine the finished dessert.

But the food industry found another way to improve the process: start with a pumpkin better suited to the job.

That is where Libby’s, one of the country’s largest canned-pumpkin producers, and the Dickinson pumpkin enter the story.

In a recent development, according to Libby’s, farmer Elijah Dickinson brought special Dickinson pumpkin seeds from Kentucky to Illinois in 1835. The variety became closely associated with commercial pumpkin processing, and Libby, McNeill & Libby acquired Dickinson & Co. in 1929, strengthening the company’s connection to the crop.

Dickinson pumpkins look different from the bright orange pumpkins sold for carving (often called field pumpkins). Their tan skin matters less to processors than the dense flesh beneath it. Relatively high in solids and sugars, Dickinson pumpkins are particularly well-suited to puree.

Many carving pumpkins, by contrast, have stringier flesh that makes them harder to process into a smooth puree. Coupland explains that they are not ideally suited to commercial food production because their fibers can be difficult to break down.

Recent findings suggest that coupland describes Dickinson puree as having a “smooth, even texture,” adding that it means you won’t be “picking fibers out of your teeth.” Rather than trying to eliminate the stringiness of a carving pumpkin, processors can start with a variety whose natural characteristics make the job easier. The raw material itself becomes part of the technology.

Libby’s helped bring this approach into American kitchens through its canned-pumpkin business, pairing a suitable variety with industrial processing to deliver consistent puree to home bakers.

In a recent development, interestingly, Dickinson pumpkins belong to Cucurbita moschata, a species that includes several varieties of winter squash. Many familiar carving pumpkins belong to Cucurbita pepo. Botanically, the distinction between pumpkin and squash is largely a matter of common usage rather than a strict scientific boundary. The FDA permits certain sweet, golden-fleshed squashes to be labeled as pumpkin in canned products, reflecting the longstanding overlap in how the terms are used in the food trade.

For pumpkin pie, what matters most is the flesh inside: how it tastes, how it breaks down, and how consistently it performs. Today’s Thanksgiving cooks no longer needs to work themselves to the bone because the food industry has learned to do the work first.

While the three-row GV80 has been a fixture in the luxury SUV segment for several years, the GV80 Hybrid is new for 2028. A turbocharged four-cylinder and a pair of electric motors combine for 347 horsepower and drive either the rear or all four wheels through a seven-speed automatic transmission. Genesis engineered the transmission without a reverse gear, instead opting to utilize the electric motors to back the GV80 Hybrid up.

Sources indicate that first Row: The GV80’s cabin is first class, highly stylish, and swathed in top-grade materials. Genesis combines the GV80’s infotainment screen and gauge cluster into one 27.0-inch OLED display perched atop a sleek and simple dashboard. Every GV80 also comes with wireless smartphone charging, a Wi-Fi hotspot, and wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay integration.

Genesis provides one of the most generous standard safety suites in the class. Every GV80 gets blind-spot monitoring, front and rear parking sensors, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control with a hands-free driving mode.

For information about the GV80 Hybrid’s crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.
  • In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.
  • Toyota initially stated about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.

In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.

Toyota initially stated about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

According to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.

Sources indicate that the problem stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.

Toyota said the issue occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.

When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.

Following an internal investigation, Toyota said in the NHTSA report that the issue was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.

The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.

OTA would be great, but there are some systems that are isolated and can't be updated that way. The EV-ECU is a core function system that is very likely sealed to prevent tampering. They never expected to need to reprogram it. It's like the firmware on your phone.

Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.

Toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.

Recent findings suggest that other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet declared next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.

Sources indicate that check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

The Game Awards 2025 ceremony brought us yet more gacha game news, this time a massive announcement for Arknights: Endfield. The free-to-play game set in the the universe of Arknights has been in various forms of closed tests for a while, but it finally has a release date.

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a new OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

If you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build revealed off polished content, with upcoming animations and cutscenes.

It has been revealed that we’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

Nearly 1 In 5 Tesla Model Ys Failed Their First German Inspection

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (618 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty rapidly.
  • Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026.
  • The Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ask a used Tesla buyer what they’d like checked first, and I’m pretty sure the battery would come up pretty rapidly. After reading what German inspectors found underneath some surprisingly young Model Ys, I’d want to know how the suspension was holding up, too.

Germany’s TÜV analyzed 9.7 million mandatory roadworthiness inspections carried out between July 2025 and June 2026. The most revealing comparison was among cars coming in for their first check, at around three years old. EVs won three of the six vehicle classes, but they also occupied the bottom three spots in the overall ranking.

The Model Y finished last out of 109 models for the second year running. Inspectors found major defects on 18.5% of the Model Ys they checked, up from 17.3% a year earlier and nearly triple the 6.4% average for cars that age. No model in that age group recorded a worse result since the 2015 report. Meanwhile, just 3% of Mazda MX-30 EVs failed, good enough for third overall behind the Mazda CX-60 and Mercedes-Benz GLA.

For the Model Y, inspectors flagged worn suspension joints 24 times as often as they did on comparable cars. They also found defective brake discs on 3.4% of Model Ys, against a 1% average for the age group. Front lighting drew more complaints than usual, too.

Tesla Model Ys covered more miles than average, though. By the time they demonstrated up for inspection, the Model Ys had traveled an average of 36,000 miles (58,000 kilometers). The average car in the group had driven 29,200 miles (47,000 km), and the average MX-30 had covered only 16,200 miles (26,000 km). Those Teslas had driven more than twice as far as the Mazdas in roughly the same amount of time.

Sources indicate that the MG4 is the first car from a Chinese automaker to appear in the report, and it finished second from the bottom, with a 16% failure rate despite averaging only 23,000 miles (37,000 km). Inspectors flagged brake discs on 10.3% of MG4s, about ten times the average. Suspension defects were also unusually common. Just ahead of the MG was Tesla’s Model 3, with a 12.5% failure rate at an average of 34,200 miles (55,000 km).

It has been revealed that the Model Y’s poor performance in Germany runs counter to its reputation for reliability. American buyers may remember that Consumer Reports ranked the Model Y as its most reliable fresh EV, though that’s based on owners reporting the problems they’d encountered.

According to recent reports, technical inspections, on the other hand, may find play in a suspension joint that the driver hasn’t noticed. There’s also a difference between buying latest and buying used, even in Consumer Reports’ own data. Tesla finished last as a brand in its separate survey of five- to ten-year-old cars, which is perhaps more telling.

The German results apply to the Model Y that preceded the Juniper refresh. When I drove the updated Model Y, the softer suspension and new frequency-selective dampers made it noticeably more comfortable. Whether this softer suspension setup holds up better is something we’ll learn as those cars cover more miles.

  • Sources indicate that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence.
  • Sources indicate that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

Sources indicate that the US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

Sources indicate that texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

According to recent reports, utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of newly introduced capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” mentioned Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, Newly introduced York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

Industry observers note that the US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Sources indicate that solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

You wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

The article is good with the reporting about grid tied storage, but seems to miss the forest for the trees with it comes to pricing. Texas isn't installing more grid tied storage because of altruistic intent.

According to recent reports, the storage is being added because they electricity suppliers can use it to make money. They can make money because we have a reasonably well thought out wholesale electrical market AND because that market has purchases large amounts of solar and wind generation.

Sources indicate that that combination means that I still pay just $0.01 more per kwh than I did when I moved to this state 20 years ago. I pay 12 cents per kwh and Texas average is between 12 and 15. A functional market is what makes that work.

Industry observers note that more than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty states the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

Recent findings suggest that I reviewed the StickerPix Print + Cut in October and I have made a ton of stickers ever since. My daughter in college has also chewed through a ton of my paper, which is a glowing recommendation since she hates pretty much everything. You can grab that printer and its Essential Bundle for $249.00 (was $299.00) in the Cricut sale at Amazon. The StickerPix Print, which skips the blade, is $119.00 (was $169.00), which is a great deal if you don’t mind buying pre-cut sheets. The rest of the list covers cutting machines, heat presses and the vinyl, iron-on and cardstock you’ll run through fastest. If you’re into making stuff and crafting, you’ll want to jump on these deals and stock up while you can.

The PopSci Proven sticker printer that cuts its own work.

Recent findings suggest that I tested the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut in October, and setup took less than 10 minutes. The Essential Bundle is $249.00 (was $299.00). It’s a dye-sublimation printer with a blade inside, so it prints a 4 x 7-inch sheet and then kiss-cuts each sticker without slicing through the backing. A few of my stickers survived an accidental trip through the dishwasher. It only works with Cricut’s own paper and ink packs, so plan on buying refills. It earned a PopSci Proven award, and my full StickerPix Print + Cut review covers the paper costs and the quirks.

The same printing tech without the blade, for $130 less.

The Cricut StickerPix Print drops the cutting blade and $130 of the price. It’s $119.00 (was $169.00). Cricut claims it uses the same dye-sublimation printing as the StickerPix Print + Cut, but the stickers come on pre-cut sheets, so the shapes are set before you print. It also turns out 4 x 6-inch photo prints. Pick this one if you mostly want labels, round stickers and snapshots and don’t need custom outlines.

A compact cutter sized for printer-paper sticker sheets.

A sheet of printer paper is 8.5 inches wide, and that’s the width Cricut lists for the Cricut Joy Xtra, which is $129.00 (was $179.00) for Black Friday. The sizing is deliberate. This machine can cut around full-color stickers you’ve printed on a regular inkjet, and Cricut claims it works with more than 50 materials, including vinyl, iron-on and cardstock. Cuts top out at 4 feet long, so it handles labels, cards and T-shirt designs, but big wall decals belong on a larger machine.

A 12-inch cutter that’s smaller than the last Explore.

Cricut states the Explore 5 is 30 percent smaller than the machine it replaced, and it kept the 12-inch cutting width. The Cricut Explore 5 Essential Bundle with digital content is $199.00 (was $249.00). It takes the same 12 x 12-inch mats as earlier Explore and Maker machines. Cricut lists more than 100 compatible materials for it, and it can cut Smart Materials up to 12 feet long without a mat, which is the reason to pick it over a Joy if banners or large decals are in your plans.

A palm-size press for the spots a big one can’t reach.

It has been revealed that shoes, stuffed animals, seams and the gaps between shirt buttons are all bad places for a full-size heat press. The Cricut EasyPress Mini in Raspberry is built for them, and it’s $39.00 (was $49.99). Cricut gives it three heat settings, a ceramic-coated plate, an insulated base to rest it on and an automatic shutoff. It’s also the least expensive machine in this post.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.
  • It’s always a massive deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a massive deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

Sources indicate that the first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

Recent findings suggest that the expansion adds a upcoming region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a substantial overhaul, headlined by the new War Looks feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The newly introduced endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with upcoming bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The average car has about 30,000 pieces, if you count individual nuts and bolts. It’s difficult enough to put all of that together, but it’s even more difficult to make it look good. While there are plenty of decent-looking new cars on the market, the ones that go above and beyond in the design department truly shimmer. You’ll notice that our preferences trend towards sports cars, but we’ve also included plenty of sedans, a single SUV, and a wide range of price points. Among the plethora of vehicles that have cycled through our office, here are our picks for the best-looking cars on the market today.

Every Brand Still Selling Sports Cars | Our Top-Rated Car Brands | Future Cars Worth Waiting For.

According to recent reports, nothing turns a head quite like a Ferrari, and we think the mid-engined 296 is the stunner of the current lineup. It looks fantastic as both a coupe and as a convertible. The active rear spoiler manages to maintain the sports car’s sleek profile whether it’s engaged or not, and the low nose with a thin, sweeping grille is classic Ferrari. The 296 drives as good as it looks, too, thanks to its hybrid powertrain that uses a twin-turbo V-6 engine.

Recent findings suggest that the Miata has been an enthusiast staple since it entered the market wide-eyed and grinning in 1990. Since then, it’s grown up a bit, replacing pop-up headlights with angular, cat-like eyes and turning the grin into a bit more of a snarl. It’s a head-turner in any generation, but the newest ND is the sportiest model yet, and it’s best enjoyed with the top down. We also love the look of the Retractable Fastback (RF) body style pictured here. For an incredibly fun and affordable sports car, the Miata is truly always the answer.

More About the Mazda MX-5 Miata.

While the Genesis brand isn’t quite as well-established as Mercedes or BMW, its flagship G90 looks every bit the part of a luxury sedan. Thin, sweeping taillights punctuate the nicely shaped rear end, while the classic diamond-shaped grille integrates beautifully with the slim, low-profile headlights. The G90 looks, sounds, and feels silky, and its sub-$100,000 starting price tag is surprising given how special it is.

Like the G90, the GV70’s sophisticated design language helps it punch above its weight against the Porsches and Mercedes-Benzes in its segment. The GV70’s sporty body lines and interior details, including a knurled glass shift knob, make it feel like a true luxury vehicle. Genesis added a Prestige Graphite trim to the lineup for 2027, which makes the GV70 look even sportier with carbon-fiber pieces, darkened trim, and red brake calipers.

According to recent reports, when Maserati brought back the GranTurismo nameplate in 2024, the sports car got a subtle redesign that brought out all of the best qualities found in the previous generation. Since then, it’s only gotten better thanks to a styling refresh for 2027. With a cheerfully aggressive front end and a sloped, sleek rear that tapers nicely, the GranTurismo coupe exudes high-performance fun in a stylish two-door package.

More About the Maserati GranTurismo.

The Lotus Emira looks great from any angle, and its gorgeously proportioned styling rivals much more expensive exotics. The Emira is a true stripped-back sports car, with just the necessities inside the cabin and a heavy focus on performance and agility. It’s unmistakably a mid-engined car, as the rear fenders flare out to make room for the hefty air intakes behind the doors, and the sleek roofline melts seamlessly into an angular rear end for a spunky-yet-elegant silhouette.

Lucid recently took pole position in our top-ranked car brands list, and both the Air and the Gravity SUV have won our 10Best award in the past. Beyond its stunning performance, the Lucid Air’s styling promotes a sense of practical luxury that looks upscale without shouting about it. Modern-looking light signatures at the front and rear lean into minimalistic design trends, and the sedan’s interior looks just as stealthy as its exterior.

The muscular Vantage is full of British charm as either a coupe or as a roadster. Its long-hood, short-deck proportions perfectly complement the twin-turbo V-8 under the hood, and the cabin looks tastefully upscale. The detailing is exquisite, too. There’s a reason James Bond’s car of choice is so often an Aston Martin.

More About the Aston Martin Vantage.

Industry observers note that the current Nissan Z brings the gorgeous 240Z of the past into the modern day while preserving much of its original characteristics. There’s also a hint of the 300ZX in its taillight shape. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill.
  • “This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.
  • Recent findings suggest that the wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight tech giant Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In March, we reported on a bobcat who endured a four-hour surgery on two broken legs after getting hit and dragged by a car, after her head had gotten stuck in the car’s grill. During a strangely similar scenario, the same wildlife center in Pennsylvania recently treated a great horned owl (Bubo virginianus) who also got jammed in the front of a vehicle. But this one was dragged along for 70 miles.

“This is a very unusual case, as most animals that are hit by a tractor-trailer die due to their injuries or are killed instantly,” Tracie Young, director of Raven Ridge Wildlife Center tells Popular Science.

Recent findings suggest that the wildlife center’s team received a voicemail from cargo and freight tech giant Old Dominion Freight Line, saying that one of their drivers in Pennsylvania had hit an owl. When they called back, they discovered that the owl was alive and had gotten stuck in the truck’s air dam. The company’s maintenance team was able to remove the owl, but something was clearly wrong with the bird because it couldn’t fly away.

The wildlife team told them to place the injured animal in a dark and quiet place. Ultimately, transport volunteers were able to transfer the owl to Raven Ridge, where the team had waited to receive the patient past the wildlife center’s closing hours. Its feathers were a mess, but the staff was shocked to find no broken wings or legs, nor open wounds. The owl had just injured its left eye.

According to recent reports, but when they called back the next day, “the story got even more incredible,” according to the wildlife center. The driver had felt the collision, but she didn’t know that the owl had gotten stuck on the truck, so she’d continued driving all the way back to the terminal.

In a recent development, “The distance from the spot where the owl was hit to the terminal was 70 miles,” the team wrote.“The owl was stuck headfirst in the fiberglass air dam for 70 miles at 65 miles per hour. It’s truly the luckiest owl we’ve ever seen.”.

According to recent reports, staff brought the hardy survivor to their vet for an eye exam, which revealed blood and swelling in the injured eye. The wildlife team is now monitoring the bird’s recovery.

Industry observers note that “The owl is doing great, and the left eye that sustained the damage is also healing. After we move the owl outside into a flight cage, we will make sure that the owl can sustain flight, that there are no obvious underlying issues, and that it can find the food placed in its cage,” Young concludes.

The goal is to ultimately release it close to where the collision occurred.

Americans Bought More Used EVs In October. Fewer Of Them Were Teslas

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • September was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y.
  • Sources indicate that americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive.
  • Cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

September was a good month to be selling a used Tesla Model Y. Sales jumped nearly 14% from August, and the Ford Mustang Mach-E did even better. The Chevrolet Equinox EV beat both, though, with a nearly 42% increase. A month later, only one of those three electric crossovers was still gaining buyers: the Chevy.

Sources indicate that americans bought an estimated 48,678 used EVs in October, according to the latest EV Market Monitor from Cox Automotive. That’s up 4.7% from September and 73.2% year over year. Used Tesla sales, meanwhile, fell 5.4% from September, with the Model 3, Model Y, and Model X losing ground.

Cox says used EV sales rose 4.7% from September to October. However, its September report put sales at 47,862 vehicles. October’s total of 48,678 is 816 higher, which is a 1.7% gain; Cox doesn’t explain the discrepancy.

Industry observers note that tesla still dominated the used EV scene, though. The change was one spot down, with Chevrolet moving ahead of Ford into second place. Hyundai and BMW rounded out the top five. The Equinox EV and Blazer EV added to their September gains, while the Kia EV6, Nissan Leaf and Volkswagen ID.4 also found more buyers than in the previous month.

Cox states this is because a growing supply of cars coming off lease is giving shoppers more choices across brands and price points.

It has been revealed that that 73% jump over last year deserves a little context. October 2025 was the first full month after the federal EV tax credit ended and Americans bought about 30,000 used EVs. In March, sales hit a record of nearly 43,000. EVs made up 3.3% of U.S. used car sales in October, matching September’s record and up from 2% a year earlier.

For used EV shoppers, the more useful number might be $36,582. That was the average asking price for a used EV in October, down from $36,767 in September and 1.9% below a year earlier. The Equinox EV, ID.4, Mach-E and Nissan Ariya all got cheaper.

Used Teslas didn’t for a second consecutive month, rising 1.8% to an average of $34,109. Even after that increase, the average used Tesla was listed for about $2,500 less than the average used EV.

It has been revealed that used EVs still carried a $2,236 premium over gas cars and hybrids, up slightly from $2,137 in September. Dealers had 38 days’ worth of used EVs on hand at October’s sales pace, versus 47 days for gas cars and hybrids.

At October’s sales pace, traditional dealers had enough used Teslas to last 32 days, the shortest supply of any major brand Cox tracked. Cox’s count leaves out Tesla’s own stores. Another study looked at how long each used EV spent on dealer lots in September. The Audi Q4 E-Tron Sportback sold the fastest, and no Tesla made the top ten.

Over on the fresh-car side, Americans bought 83,262 EVs in October, down 3.9% from September but up 3% from a year earlier, marking the first year-over-year gain of 2026. EVs’ share of new sales slipped from 6.5% in September to 6.2% last month. The average buyer paid $56,221 for a new EV, even with incentives averaging $6,375 per vehicle. Dealers had 85 days’ supply of new EVs, more than double their used inventory.

October wasn’t all bad for Tesla. While sales of second-hand Model Ys fell, Americans bought 36,366 brand-new examples, up 9.4% from September. It accounted for nearly 44% of all new EVs sold in the country.

#17646. Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia

Tiny egg-eating snake discovered in Ethiopia

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (372 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that biologists have discovered multiple upcoming species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains.
  • “Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), mentioned in a statement.
  • Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that biologists have discovered multiple upcoming species of egg-eating snakes slithering through the forests near southeastern Ethiopia’s Bale Mountains. Although researchers only described the white-throated egg-eater (Dasypeltis albigularis) in their study recently published in the journal Herpetozoa, they promised that information on additional finds is on the way.

“Three other species in this genus are still waiting in line,” Arthur Tiutenko, a study co-author and herpetologist at Germany’s Friedrich-Alexander University of Erlangen–Nuremberg (FAU), mentioned in a statement.

Many snakes will snack on an egg if the opportunity presents itself. But for a handful of species, it’s all eggs, all the time. These nonvenomous snakes solely eat shelled embryos, and largely exist in Africa and some portions of India. To devour their meals, egg-eating snakes have evolved a set of very clever biological tricks. First, their back bones extend all the way into their esophagus and function like a saw to slice open shells. From there, the snake’s neck muscles contract and funnel the egg contents down its throat. Once finished, the reptile simply spits out the cracked shells.

However, Tiutenko’s team almost missed D. albigularis entirely. At first glance, the snake looks extremely similar to a species called the montane egg-eater (Dasypeltis atra). A closer inspection revealed some key differences—a patch of white scales extending down its stomach earned its “white-throated” moniker, while the skin between each scale has a distinctly blue shimmer. Other egg-eating snakes can rub their scales to create a rustling noise that startles foes, but only the D. albigularis females do the same—and they do it silently.

In a recent development, don’t envision python-sized snakes chowing down on chicken eggs though. D. albigularis is less than eight inches long, weighs only 0.05 ounces, and is about as thick as a knitting needle. This means the snakes only have eyes for particularly tiny eggs from various diminutive birds. Luckily, their regional home is full of options.

“That may also be the reason why egg-eating snakes only live in Africa, and in particular in a small area in the southwest corner of the Arabian peninsula,” added Tiutenko.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next major thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” mentioned founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

Recent findings suggest that “This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”.

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

Go back the several years that Musk told us about the limitations of LiDAR. Tesla was having it's own problems with Cameras and RADAR at the time. Musk objected to LiDAR, pointing out its limitations. At the time it appeared to make sense. LiDAR was expensive and the performance was at a certain level. But the occasionally visionary Elon wasn't particularly visionary on that occasion or every time he repeated his stance. Truth is, Cameras were cheaper, and computer performance wasn't wasn't going to get there if all the added complexity was loading it up. So Tesla ditched RADAR and only briefly considered LiDAR. I could say that Musk never considered it at all, but then he truly would have been a fool to base an opinion on nothing but his untested perception. But LiDAR got better and it got a lot, lot cheaper, and anyway, Tesla's HW3 wasn't going to cut it either. HW4 looks like it may have a tough time for 99.999% safety. Thing is, eyesight can't deal with every single situation, and neither can cameras. So if you want to get as close to 100% safety as possible, these days it seems a bit silly to leave aside LiDAR. But Elon has dug his heels in, and won't be going back on that decision from years ago. Maybe FSD might have got there quicker with LiDAR. Maybe not. And what of HW3.? That was going to take owners to FSD years ago. And people paid big money for it. I hear there's a fresh option as of Sept 2026, swapping out all the kit and cameras for HW4. Perhaps wait for HW5.?

Resilience and perseverance was on full display in Alaska this summer. The park rangers at Tongass National Forest in the southeastern corner of the state spotted an unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) with a broken arm. Even with this injury, the tough bear still managed to catch the fish running through Anan Creek. For this grit, the rangers awarded the bear with the 2026 Grin & Bear It Award.

Sources indicate that “We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write. “In other wild places the injury may have been a death sentence, but the abundance of Anan gives this bear a chance.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Industry observers note that the largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

Industry observers note that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears like the one with the broken arm and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their portly counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own behaviors and quirks.

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is adorable and I want one. Hedley Studios in the UK just came out with a replica Porsche 550 Spyder, which itself isn't a unique idea. There have been Volkswagen-powered 550 Spyder replicas for decades. What sets this one apart are two things: one is that it's only 80% scale, so it's a little fella, and the other is that it's electric. It's called the Porsche 550 J (for Junior) it looks like a blast.

I can't tell if the 550 J is a track toy or just a toy, but either way it looks like fun. At 80% scale, it looks positively bite-sized next to the real one, which was already one of the smallest production road cars you'll ever see. So it's tiny. So much so, in fact, that I struggle to see how two adults can actually fit in its two seats side-by-side. And, as you'd imagine with such a tiny footprint, the 550 J isn't road legal and is only meant for private roads and race track.

Like a real 550 Spyder, all of the 550 J's weight is behind the driver. Two 1.8 kWh battery packs provide the juice at 48 volts, while a single 11 horsepower electric motor drives the rear wheels. It only weighs 728 pounds, so that power should be enough to have some fun with. Add two passengers, though, and its weight can pretty easily pass the half-ton mark. At that point, 11 horses isn't much. However, there is an optional RS pack that bumps it to 21 horsepower. Top speed also jumps from 40 mph to 50 mph.

The RS Pack also adds two more of those 1.8 kWh battery packs, though, which adds another 44 pounds. That weight penalty might be worth it for the range, though. The standard 550 J only has 30 miles of range, while the RS has 50. That isn't a lot but it's enough for a track day. Plus, with such small batteries, the 550 J will charge up promptly. Lap the track a bunch of times, plug it in and have some lunch, and get back to it.

Recent findings suggest that track days should be fun, too. Bilstein dampers with Eibach springs handle suspension duty, while Brembo brakes do the stopping. The RS model gets Bilstein adjustable coilovers and drilled brake rotors, too. So despite having Power Wheels-levels of horsepower, it has genuine track car handling bits.

Sources indicate that hedley has done an admirable job of making the 550 J look like a real 550 Spyder that was hit with a shrink ray. It's smaller, sure, but you wouldn't know it from photos. Everything about it looks spot on, from every exterior detail of its carbon fiber body, to the interior switchgear, and even the fuel filler cap. It's a very impressive recreation and one that will look fantastic in owners' garages. Hedley claims it worked closely with the Porsche Museum to get all the details right and it shows.

Only 250 of these will be made, and they'll cost £69,500 ($91,406) each. So it isn't cheap, especially for something that isn't road legal. However, for folks who can afford to spend that kind of cash on a track day toy, this seems like a really fun way to do it.

The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1091 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home.
  • The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran.
  • “While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” said IEA executive director Fatih Birol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the big takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) new “World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.

The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran. Well-stocked oil inventories helped buffer the initial shock, and the IEA coordinated a release of emergency oil reserves. Some Gulf oil took routes around the strait. Atlantic Basin exporters shipped more, and China sharply cut its crude imports. Now more of the burden is falling on consumers, who are paying higher prices and cutting back.

“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” said IEA executive director Fatih Birol.

The IEA has seen EV sales jump in some countries hit by the crisis, along with increased trade in solar panels and batteries. For countries that import a lot of oil and gas, switching to EVs and heat pumps can help reduce their exposure to the next fuel price spike.

Industry observers note that “The impact of Hormuz is only just beginning to become clear,” noted energy think tank Ember’s chief analyst Dave Jones. “Hormuz will speed up electrification and renewables, likely faster than many people think. So much of the momentum for electrification at COP31 comes from the desire to have cheaper and more secure energy.”.

It has been revealed that solar leads renewables growth in every scenario the IEA models, and nuclear power is growing strongly, too. Energy efficiency and biofuels could also gain ground. The push to use more homegrown energy could have a very different effect in parts of Asia, where some countries that import oil and gas have plenty of their own coal and could keep burning it for longer.

The world was already using a lot more electricity before the crisis. Since 2019, electricity demand has grown twice as fast as overall energy demand, outpacing global economic growth. Everything from industrial motors and air conditioners to EVs, heat pumps, and data centers is driving that growth. Electricity comes close to 30% of the energy the world actually uses by 2035 in each of the IEA’s exploratory scenarios.

Sources indicate that before the crisis, around 20 million barrels of oil a day moved through the Strait of Hormuz. If shipping stays risky, upcoming pipelines could route some of those barrels around the strait, while buyers turn to other suppliers or use less oil. In that case, the IEA says the amount of oil that needs to pass through Hormuz could drop to 8.5 million barrels a day in 2030 and below 2 million by 2035. The Middle East would still be the world’s largest oil-exporting region.

Recent findings suggest that if the conflict is resolved, oil and gas supply could bounce back. A delayed wave of liquefied natural gas could also help bring prices down even as buyers refill their inventories. Faster electrification could take some of the demand out of both markets.

In a recent development, the world is now using more energy to cool its buildings than to heat them for the first time, the IEA indicates. By 2035, the global population is expected to grow by 650 million and the economy by a third. Energy needs rise gradually in advanced economies, growth slows in China, and India and Southeast Asia lead faster increases across other emerging and developing economies.

Then there’s AI. Under the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, global data center electricity use doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030. That buildout is already running into grid and supply chain constraints, and in some places, local opposition. The IEA also flags risks to critical mineral supplies and threats to energy infrastructure from natural hazards and cyberattacks.

Energy-related CO2 emissions stay around today’s levels under current policies. They start to fall under stated policies and drop further in the IEA’s Additional Response Case, which looks at what could happen if governments respond more strongly to the crisis. Even those deeper cuts fall short of what climate goals require. The current and stated policy scenarios point to 2.5C to 2.9C of warming, and the latest round of national climate pledges shows little sign that countries are speeding up energy-sector emissions cuts.

According to recent reports, the green agenda always come in a second place because people cannot see that far out in the future. Stability of the economy and energy independence are much more key drivers and have immediate impact. Local environment boosts like clean air in cities are also immediate drivers while long term reduced medical bills are not. The oil industry is challenged becuase, unlike previous numerous crises, there is an alternative and the green is the upcoming black.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a more immediate cost, too. More people gained access to electricity and clean cooking in 2025, but higher fuel prices and shortages threaten to slow that progress. Around 720 million people still live without electricity, and nearly 2 billion cook with polluting fuels or technologies.

Psychedelic therapies may improve decision making

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health concerns like anxiety and depression.
  • The team’s experiment was straightforward.
  • While the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health concerns like anxiety and depression. Although they’re commonly associated with mind-altering trips and sometimes confounding experiences, recent research indicates small doses may provide an opposite outcome. In a study published today in the journal Science Advances, researchers show that psychedelics may actually improve decision making in certain situations.

The team’s experiment was straightforward. After supplying lab mice with small amounts of ketamine or psilocybin, neuroscientists exposed them to a simple, sensory-based training exercise. Each mouse was tasked with identifying which of two sites contained a reward based on light pulses emitted from either location. Researchers then compared their decisions with a control group of mice who didn’t receive either psychedelic.

While the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue. However, the mice treated with ketamine or psilocybin appeared to rely less on repetition and more on sensory observations. As a result, they had fewer errors and found the location more effectively.

“These findings reveal how psychedelics reduce the reliance on habits and repetitive choices, which may explain part of their therapeutic effect,” Benjamin Scott, a Boston University psychologist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.

According to recent reports, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) have remained the most commonly prescribed anxiety and depression medications for decades, but they often come with caveats. Patients usually take SSRIs for weeks before experiencing any relief, and they must take them consistently for indefinite periods of time. Meanwhile, about 30 percent of people with depression are resistant to SSRIs, which makes treatment much more difficult. Another benefit is that the effects of ketamine and psilocybin are much easier to map in the brain compared to SSRIs, even after a half century of research.

“We know a great deal about how psychedelics affect the nervous system,” noted Scott.

On a molecular level, psychedelics bind to receptors on neurons, protective neural cells called glia, and likely other cells. Once attached, the effects compound throughout the brain by altering cellular activity, circuits, and neuroactivity. Psilocybin works with serotonin receptors to influence how information is processed. In contrast, ketamine is a dissociative psychedelic that functions as an antagonist to specific receptors.

In a recent development, “The discovery we report in this paper is that these two drugs have similar pro-cognitive effects, at least in mice performing a simple task,” Scott explained. “Both drugs strengthen the influence of sensory evidence on choices and reduce the effect of bias.”.

The study’s authors do note some potentially negative effects, as well. Although a mouse’s accuracy improved, the correct decisions sometimes came more slowly than before they took the psychedelics. Scott remarked this may logically translate to impacts on human reaction times, which could be a problem during activities like driving a car or playing sports. Despite this, the team is still confident in what psychedelics have already accomplished for patients, as well as what that could mean in the future. Scott cited existing evidence of patients reporting noticeable, long-lasting improvements after a single dose of psilocybin.

“This is dramatically different than today’s first-line drugs for depression,” he added.

#17636. Industry News: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event

📅 15 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1258 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: NASA warns this year's Monster El Niño could be even bigger than legendary 1997 event

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1258 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA scientists are tracking an exceptionally powerful El Niño that could grow even larger than the historic 1997 event, which brought extreme weather to regions around the world.
  • According to recent reports, el Niño is a recurring climate phenomenon that typically develops every two to seven years, when ocean temperatures rise above normal across parts of the equatorial Pacific.
  • Two of the most powerful recent El Niño events occurred in 1997-98 and 2015-16.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA scientists are tracking an exceptionally powerful El Niño that could grow even larger than the historic 1997 event, which brought extreme weather to regions around the world. Using 35 years of satellite observations, researchers can now compare the rapidly developing 2026 El Niño with some of the strongest events ever recorded, revealing remarkable similarities and important differences.

According to recent reports, el Niño is a recurring climate phenomenon that typically develops every two to seven years, when ocean temperatures rise above normal across parts of the equatorial Pacific. These changes can disrupt atmospheric circulation and alter weather patterns far beyond the Pacific Ocean.

Two of the most powerful recent El Niño events occurred in 1997-98 and 2015-16. Both had widespread consequences, including destructive fires in Indonesia and the Amazon, severe drought and crop failures in southern Africa, and intense rainfall and coastal flooding in Southern California. Now, the 2026 El Niño is emerging as another major event, with satellite data suggesting it could rival those historic episodes.

How El Niño Builds Strength in the Pacific.

The development of El Niño depends on a complex interaction between ocean temperatures and atmospheric winds.

Sources indicate that under normal conditions, steady trade winds push warm surface water toward the western Pacific Ocean. This causes warm water to accumulate in the west, where the ocean surface sits slightly higher than it does farther east.

When the trade winds weaken, some of that warm water begins moving eastward across the Pacific. The shift can weaken the winds even further or occasionally cause them to reverse direction. This allows additional warm water to spread east, reinforcing the process and raising ocean temperatures and sea levels across the central and eastern Pacific.

According to recent reports, although the underlying process is similar each time, no two El Niño events develop in exactly the same way. Their behavior depends partly on where the warmest water accumulates and how the atmosphere responds to the changing ocean conditions.

"The search for the 'typical' El Niño is very elusive," said Josh Willis, project scientist for sea level missions at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). "They're all different in terms of where they land and how their impacts play out.".

NASA Satellites Reveal Striking Similarities to 1997.

To understand how the current El Niño compares with earlier events, scientists are examining decades of satellite measurements of ocean surface height.

This technique, called satellite altimetry, measures subtle changes in the elevation of the ocean surface. Because seawater expands as it becomes warmer, unusually high sea levels in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific can reveal where heat is accumulating during El Niño.

Recent findings suggest that NASA's comparison maps show differences in Pacific Ocean surface height on October 13, 1997 (left), and October 12, 2026 (right). The earlier measurements were collected by the TOPEX/Poseidon satellite, while the newer observations came from the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite. Scientists at JPL processed both datasets to make the events easier to compare.

The maps use red to identify areas where the ocean surface is higher than its usual level, while white represents normal conditions and blue demonstrates areas where sea levels are below average. To better isolate the effects of El Niño and other temporary natural changes, researchers removed variations associated with seasonal patterns and long-term trends.

One major advantage of these observations is their remarkable consistency. Successive satellite missions have followed nearly identical paths, with overlapping periods of operation that allow scientists to compare measurements across decades.

According to recent reports, "What's unique about altimetry is that we have a 35-year record from nearly identical satellites flying almost the same ground track, with each mission overlapping the next," Willis said. "That lets us look back in time and compare this El Niño to what happened in 1997. And right now, this one is on track to be even bigger.".

Why the 2026 El Niño Resembles a Historic Climate Giant.

In a recent development, the 2026 El Niño intensified much more abruptly than the powerful 1997-98 event. Despite that difference in timing, NASA's satellite measurements from October reveal striking similarities in how the two events are developing.

Recent findings suggest that in both cases, the Pacific displays a pronounced difference in sea level (low in the west and high in the east). The observations also show elevated, unusually warm water stretching eastward along the equator until it reaches the coast of South America.

These similarities suggest that the 2026 event could produce weather effects resembling those experienced during the 1997-98 El Niño. That earlier episode brought substantial rainfall to California and other parts of the southern United States, raising the possibility of comparable conditions during the coming winter.

However, the powerful 2015-16 El Niño demonstrates why similarities in overall strength do not necessarily translate into identical weather impacts.

For that comparison, NASA scientists also examined ocean surface height measurements from October 12, 2015, recorded by the Jason-2 satellite. The data were placed alongside observations from approximately the same time of year in 1997 and 2026.

Although the 2015 event also featured exceptionally warm water and elevated sea levels along the equator, that warm water did not extend toward the South American coast as strongly as it did during the other two events.

The resulting rainfall patterns were different as well. During the winter of 2015-16, much of the precipitation associated with El Niño was concentrated over Central America and the southeastern United States, while Mexico experienced significant flooding.

Will El Niño Bring Extreme Weather in Winter 2026-27?

The latest observations have prompted scientists to closely monitor how the 2026 El Niño develops and what it could mean for weather conditions in the months ahead.

In its October 8, 2026, outlook, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) estimated an 83 percent chance that strong to very strong El Niño conditions would occur during the first three months of 2027.

That forecast points to the potential for a particularly significant climate event, but it does not establish exactly where the most severe effects will occur.

In a recent development, el Niño can influence weather across much of the planet by changing the movement of heat and moisture through the atmosphere. However, those effects become increasingly difficult to predict farther from the tropical Pacific, where other atmospheric processes can alter or weaken the expected patterns.

As a result, even the strong resemblance between the 2026 and 1997 events cannot guarantee that the coming winter will unfold in the same way.

"There's always a bit of a dice roll here," Willis noted. "Just because this El Niño looks like 1997 doesn't mean it will be exactly the same -- it's just our best guess at the moment.".

The unprecedented consistency of the satellite record gives researchers a valuable way to recognize familiar patterns and evaluate the scale of the developing El Niño. But whether 2026-27 ultimately matches the extreme weather of previous historic events will depend on how the ocean and atmosphere interact in the months ahead.

Industry observers note that materials provided by NASA Earth Observatory. Original written by Kathryn Hansen. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hyundai and Kia have some of the strongest hybrid lineups on the market. Why did it take so long for Genesis to get there?

Hyundai and Kia hybrids are printing money. Hybrids now account for 29% of all Hyundai sales, a proportion that has grown rapidly over the last few years. But Genesis has so far been left out of the hybrid sales bonanza. No longer. Genesis revealed the G80 and GV80 hybrids on Wednesday, finally entering the fast-growing market for premium hybrids.

The G80 and GV80 are the Genesis brand’s mid-size sedan and SUV, respectively. The G80 competes against cars like the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class and was—until recently—offered with a fully electric powertrain. That was canned after slow sales, and the GV80 SUV has always been internal-combustion only.

According to recent reports, both models come standard with a 2.5-liter turbocharged gas engine and offer twin-turbo V-6 engines as performance upgrades. The newly introduced hybrid system will slot between these two powertrains. It adds a parallel hybrid setup to the 2.5-liter turbocharged powertrain, delivering a combined total of 347 horsepower. The top-trim V6 produces 375 hp, for reference.

It has been revealed that genesis notes the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient than the four-cylinder gas model. For that G80 Hybrid, that number is 30%. Final fuel economy ratings are still to come, but that’s a sizable improvement given the extra power it comes with. And like their gas-powered siblings, all G80s and GV80s come with all-wheel-drive.

All G80 and GV80 Hybrids come standard with all-wheel drive.

Recent findings suggest that kind of. The 2.5T turbo-hybrid combo is used in other Hyundai products like the Palisade Hybrid, but it is among the newest, most sophisticated powerplants in the tech giant’s stable. But the G80 and GV80 do get some Genesis-exclusive hardware. The Genesis hybrids are the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrids to feature liquid-cooled batteries. The vast majority of traditional hybrids use small batteries that are passively air-cooled, but as we know from larger EV batteries, active cooling systems are great for long-term stability. Genesis says the cooling system also allows it to take advantage of more of the battery’s energy.

It has been revealed that fundamentally, though, the powertrain should feel similar to existing Hyundai and Kia hybrids. Unlike Honda and Toyota hybrids, HMG hybrids still use traditional transmissions rather than e-CVTs. The G80 and GV80 use a seven-speed automatic, rather than the eight-speed auto that’s employed on the gas models.

The new models offer a “Stay” mode that allows you to run the HVAC and radio for extended periods without firing the gas engine, too, and an EV mode for a limited amount of engine-off cruising.

If you want something that’s more similar to an EV driving experience, Genesis already makes two smaller electric SUVs, the GV60 and Electrified GV70. A third one, the stunning GV90, is coming soon.

Sources indicate that but if you want something like a plug-in hybrid, you’ll have to wait for the company’s extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs). EREVs—which use gasoline engines purely as generators, with no direct mechanical between the engine and wheels—are coming in 2027, Genesis confirmed at the debut event. The company says they will offer over 640 miles of combined range. EREV fans will have to wait for further details.

The rear seat of the top-trim Genesis G80 Hybrid.

But if you’re a pure hybrid fan, Genesis finally has a couple of real options. Pricing, trim details, and on-sale dates are still to come. Expect to hear more details next year.

Breaking: Electric Vehicles Now Make Up Nearly 1/3rd of Global New Car Sales: Study
